source_statement: Two distinct circles have at most two common points
forward_derivation: Common point plus distinct circumference sets gives distinct centers (III5 core). All common points have the second circle radius as their distance to its center. Equal-partner uniqueness on the first circle then bounds them by the given two distinct intersections.
contract: For any two distinct common points a,b, every common point c equals a or b. This is the full at-most-two claim and does not assume transversal intersections.
